mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi Q5 2.0 TDI / 40 TDI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost to replace an Audi Q5 2.0 TDI / 40 TDI engine typically ranges from £3,200 to £6,000 for a rebuilt unit, depending on whether it is an older EA189 or newer EA288 architecture.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of oil pump hex shaft failure in an Audi Q5 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include a sudden red oil pressure warning light, a grinding noise from the lower engine block, and immediate engine seizure if the vehicle is not stopped instantly.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi Q5 8R 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the vehicle is in good overall condition and valued above £8,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is a cost-effective alternative to buying a new premium SUV.

mainEntity.name: Does the Audi Q5 40 TDI replacement engine include quattro calibration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, any professional supply & fit service for the Audi Q5 2.0 TDI / 40 TDI must include ODIS coding to ensure the engine ECU communicates correctly with the quattro transfer case and transmission.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CNHA and DEJA engine codes in the Audi Q5 40 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CNHA is the standard 2.0L EA288 TDI (190hp) used in early FY models (2017-2020), while the DEJA is the updated EA288 Evo (204hp) featuring a 12V mild-hybrid system for the facelift models (2020-present).

historyTimeline.h2: Audi Q5 2.0 TDI / 40 TDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Q5 launched, the 2.0 TDI quickly became the backbone of the range, evolving from the EA189 architecture in the 8R generation to the highly refined EA288 and the modern "40 TDI" power badge in the FY generation.

milestones.description: CAHA, 2.0L TDI (177hp), launched in the 8R generation as the entry-level diesel workhorse.
CGLB, 2.0L TDI (190hp), introduced during the 8R facelift with improved efficiency and Euro 5 compliance.
CNHA, 2.0L TDI (190hp), carried over to the all-new FY generation on the MLB Evo platform, later adopting the "40 TDI" badge.
DEJA / DEJB, 2.0L TDI (204hp) with 12V mild-hybrid technology, launched in the FY facelift strictly under the 40 TDI badge for Euro 6d compliance.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Audi Q5 2.0 TDI / 40 TDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.h4: Oil Pump Drive & Timing Chain Failure - Why the Audi Q5 2.0 TDI (CAHA/CGLB) Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The oil pump hex shaft can snap due to wear, or the timing chain tensioner fails, resulting in sudden oil starvation or valve-to-piston interference that destroys the engine internally.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Drop sump, replace hex shaft, oil pump, and timing chain tensioner
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended as a preventative measure before catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded oil pump drive components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The only viable option if the engine has already seized or suffered valve damage

problems.recommendation: For the 8R 2.0 TDI, if the engine is still running but you suspect oil pump or chain wear, a specialist preventative kit replacement is vastly cheaper than waiting for it to seize. However, if the hex shaft has already snapped or the chain has jumped, a rebuilt engine with an uprated oil pump drive is your only reliable path forward. For the FY 40 TDI, address coolant leaks immediately; a £1,000 specialist water pump and EGR upgrade is a minor expense compared to a £4,500+ full engine replacement.

problems.h4: EGR Cooler & Water Pump Leaks - Why the Audi Q5 40 TDI (CNHA/DEJA) Wears Prematurely

repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended to prevent overheating and restore emissions compliance
